notes: Full-tier runs include the offline delegate tests, end-to-end sandbox install/sync tests, and Node syntax checks. The sandbox suite needs network access for npm and uses a throwaway HOME. rollcall's npm test runs its node:test suites on throwaway git repos under $TMPDIR (about 2 min), then the hook-latency bench on its own so parallel suites do not skew it; set ROLLCALL_BENCH_PRINT=1 to print the numbers.

ci.workflows: .github/workflows/check.yml (per PR, path-filtered; a push to main re-runs the suites only when the merge's tree differs from the PR head's)
ci.notes: Hosted Linux (ubuntu-latest, Node 24); jobs are path-filtered to keep minutes down (free on a public repo, billed rounded up to the minute on a private fork). Jobs: Changes (path filter, worklog entry for the PR, merge-skew check on pushes), Scripts (syntax, delegate, hooks, ios-sim, copy-helper, rules, release), rollcall (npm test in packages/rollcall), Supervisor (installs tmux), Install sandbox (PRs only; needs network for npm; a stand-in claude CLI answers the docsic MCP registration, since the runner has none). The mods stack needs the claude CLI and stays local. No docs gate yet: no doc declares owns: frontmatter.

stacks.name: hooks
stacks.notes: The PreToolUse and PostToolUse entries (scripts/hooks/) as Claude Code runs them, with fixture guards in a throwaway overlay: guard order, an overlay guard replacing a core one, a crashing or unloadable guard allowing while the rest run, a deny skipping rollcall, ROLLCALL_DISABLE, the tools each guard names and the matcher sync builds from them, plus deploy-watch after a merge. The core ships no guards; real ones and their tests live in an overlay.

stacks.name: ios-sim
stacks.notes: iosim's pure half (accessibility listing, element matching, simulator naming), its CLI's usage errors, and install refusing a download that fails the checksum (a fake curl in a throwaway HOME). No simulator and no AXe: driving a real simulator is checked by hand with a /ios-sim run.

stacks.name: copy-helper
stacks.notes: copy.sh, the part of kesselrunner Copy.app that does the work: the links it takes and refuses, and the text it hands pbcopy (a fake pbcopy in a throwaway folder). Building and registering the app itself is checked by hand: `node scripts/copy-helper/install.mjs --force`, then `open kesselrunner-copy://<id>` for a saved block.

stacks.name: rules
stacks.notes: `kesselrunner rules` in a throwaway HOME whose overlay holds a fixture rule (the core ships none): listing from the core and the overlay (the overlay's wins on a shared name), on and off, the CLAUDE.md block before and after, refusals, and a rule that is on but in neither. Offline: a toggle runs only the CLAUDE.md step of a sync.

stacks.name: release
stacks.notes: scripts/release.sh in a throwaway copy of the release files with a local bare origin: bump sets both versions and opens the CHANGELOG entry; tag refuses a dirty, unpushed or empty-entry main, then tags locally, prints the push, gh release and npm publish steps, and pushes nothing. Runs rollcall's npm pack --dry-run.

stacks.name: supervisor
stacks.notes: Supervisor v3 on a real tmux server (a private socket per test, ROLLCALL_TMUX_SOCKET) with a fake `claude` (KESSELRUNNER_CLAUDE_BIN) that runs its launch settings' hooks, throwaway git repos and a private ROLLCALL_HOME: start, @t3 and picks typed in, words held behind a dialog flag, delivery receipts (an item leaves on the worker's prompt hook or its transcript; no receipt means retries, then one notice), a cancelled dialog settled from the transcript, whose a prompt is (the owner's or a machine's), resume (bounded: 3 in 30 minutes), a merge while the worker is parked or exited resuming it once for its after-merge steps (the task lands when it leaves with no report), a handoff holding the merge, --fresh, the home's one watcher (ROLLCALL_WATCHER=0 keeps hooks from starting it; the tests run `watch <home>` themselves) taking steps, telling the owner plain facts and typing news into the supervisor once it is idle, a supervisor parking in place and coming back (resumed or fresh), a supervisor handing over past its context mark, the status line, notifications (ROLLCALL_NOTIFY_LOG), a trust prompt, falcon new/continue/resume and its refusals, tabs written from the status line, attach switching in place, the home's supervisor.sh detach, and a scripted front-end client (`rollcall api`) beside the Falcon end to end: it starts a task, answers its question, tells its worker, attaches to its terminal and watches its PR land while the Falcon shows the same. Needs tmux. A real worker is checked by hand: a task in a trusted repo, start.mjs, then `@t3` and a pick reaching it. The front-end e2e pins ROLLCALL_WORKER_VIEW=terminal: its stand-in Claude speaks only the terminal.

stacks.name: rollcall
stacks.notes: Includes test/needs.test.mjs: falcon's first-run check (git, tmux, Claude Code, gh and its login, Node 20, the kesselrunner launcher beside the package) and falcon refusing to start without tmux. Run `npm pack --dry-run` here after changing files or package.json: the tarball holds bin/, src/, README.md, API.md, LICENSE and package.json only. test/api.test.mjs is the front-end contract (API.md): what a front end relies on in the snapshot, the stream, the actions and attach. test/claude-worker.test.mjs runs the stream-mode worker against test/fixtures/fake-claude.mjs; test/conversation.test.mjs covers the transcript read. test/claude-contract.test.mjs checks the installed Claude Code stream flags offline; ROLLCALL_CLAUDE_CONTRACT=live adds one real Haiku turn (run it by hand after a Claude Code upgrade).

stacks.name: mods
stacks.testCommand: claude plugin validate . && for m in mods/*/; do claude plugin validate "$m" && claude plugin test "$m" || exit 1; done
stacks.notes: The marketplace file and each mod's manifest and hooks module as the engine reads them, then each mod's tests/*.test.ts against the engine itself (rollcall and gh are faked beneath the mod; no session, no login, no network). Needs Claude Code 2.1.287+ on PATH. Type-check a mod with `tsc -p mods/<name>` after loading it once with `claude --plugin-dir mods/<name>`, which lays the API's types beside it.

stacks.name: sandbox
stacks.notes: Throwaway HOME and npm prefix, real npm for docsic. Case 9 runs install.sh against a local bare origin (plain git, no gh), then again over the same clone.

stacks.name: syntax
stacks.testCommand: for f in bin/*.mjs lib/*.mjs scripts/*/*.mjs migrations/*.mjs packages/*/bin/*.mjs packages/*/src/*.mjs packages/*/src/*/*.mjs; do node --check "$f" || exit 1; done
